title: Microsoft Purview DLP: stop Copilot sending sensitive data to external web search
summary: The web-search restriction, default, commands and roadmap details are supported. Minor corrections should finish the two admin paths, simplify the Graph call, acknowledge conflicting older DLP documentation and distinguish general Purview licensing from the unpublished action-specific entitlement.

claims.claim: The web-search restriction is admin-opt-in and requires a configured DLP policy.
claims.quote: The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding. Valid values are: - $true: Web grounding is blocked. - $False: Web grounding isn't blocked. This value is the default.

claims.quote: Searched: "Performing Web Searches" licensing price meter Purview DLP; Purview DLP web search Copilot Studio licensing. Read the feature Licensing section, Purview service description and purview-billing-models; no action-specific entitlement was stated.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' for an option inside the licensed Purview product. Replace the notes with: 'Purview uses the Microsoft 365 E3/E5/A5/F5/G5 per-user licensing model for Microsoft 365 sources. claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls: first row and PowerShell paragraph
claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name <rule> -Policy <policy> -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @(@{Name="<SIT name>"}) -RestrictWebGrounding $true creates a SIT-conditioned rule that blocks web grounding.
claims.quote:
For example, `@(@{Name="U.S. Social Security Number (SSN)"; minCount="2"},@{Name="Credit Card Number"})`.
The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding.
$true: Web grounding is blocked.

claims.quote: Accounts with one of the following roles or role groups can create or edit a DLP policy for the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location: ... **Purview Data Security AI Admin** - Role for editing Data Loss Prevention policies related to Copilot

claims.quote: Searched: Copilot domain exclusion configuration admin center UI portal ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions. Read domain-exclusion and configure-copilot-admin-center; the former documents PowerShell, and the latter provides no domain-exclusion UI.

claims.claim: ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile <csv> creates a tenant domain-exclusion configuration from CSV.
claims.quote:

claims.where: controls[2].scope; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Domain exclusion is a tenant configuration that excludes selected sites from Copilot and Copilot Chat web grounding.
claims.quote: By using domain exclusion, you can specify up to 1,000 sites to exclude from web grounding in Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat through a PowerShell script. ... To manage the Copilot domain exclusion configuration for your tenant

claims.claim: When web search is enabled, Copilot may send a generated query derived from the user's prompt to Bing for grounding.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information. This generated search query is different from the user's original prompt-it consists of a few words informed by the user's prompt.

claims.claim: Purview DLP's sensitive-web-search restriction is a real-time control.
claims.quote: This real-time control helps organizations mitigate data leakage and oversharing risks by preventing Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents from using sensitive data for external web search.

claims.where: summary; What's changing: SIT condition; Governance controls
claims.claim: The web-search rule detects configured sensitive information types in prompt text.
claims.quote: Add a rule with the **Content contains** > **Sensitive information types** condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.
claims.fix: After describing the SIT condition, add: 'The general DLP policy reference still lists SIT-based content definition as unsupported for Microsoft 365 Copilot (preview), so these Microsoft pages disagree.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-policy-reference#location-support-for-how-content-can-be-defined. Keep the feature-specific SIT condition.

claims.where: What's changing: first paragraph; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The rule action is Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.
claims.quote: In the same rule, set the action to **Prevent Copilot from processing content** > **Performing Web Searches**.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: A matching web-search rule blocks external web grounding for that prompt and prevents matching prompt text from reaching external search providers.
claims.quote: This prevents prompt text that matches the configured SITs from being sent to external search providers for that request.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: Copilot still returns a response grounded in permitted internal Microsoft 365 sources after a web-search-only block.
claims.quote: Copilot still returns a response grounded in internal Microsoft 365 data sources where the user has access.

claims.claim: The sensitive-web-search restriction covers Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: **Restrict Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork from using external web search when prompts contain sensitive data.**

claims.claim: The sensitive-web-search restriction also covers Cowork.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: The roadmap extends this capability to Copilot Studio agents published to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: This capability currently extends to Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents built in Copilot Studio that are published to Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Graph as enforcing security permissions on customer content.
claims.quote: The Graph is the gatekeeper to content and plays an integral role in all Microsoft 365 interactions. It enforces the security permissions present on a customer's content and provides secure, compliant, auditable access to that content.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts run in the initiating user's security context.
claims.quote: All Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts run in the security context of the user who initiates the prompt. This means for a user to see an item in a prompt response, they must first have the necessary permissions to access the content of the item.
